model: d=3 five-round rotated Z-memory categorical circuit; gate p=.003; measurement p in [.001,.005]; burst p in [0,.002]
statistic: C in 0..5, count of five documented disjoint within-pair detector cofires
polynomial_basis: Exact rational coefficients in v=1-2*p_b and u=1-2*p_m, derived from categorical parity characters and Bernoulli subset inversion.

bernstein_partition.method: On each rectangle, every polynomial value is in the convex hull of its tensor-product Bernstein coefficients; category upper envelope is the maximum coefficient across all cells.

population_grid.purpose: Diagnostics for envelope slack and growth; continuous null validity follows from Bernstein bounds, not grid coverage.

continuous_alternative_growth_status: only calculated when --certify-alt-growth is supplied; the recorded attempt was interrupted before completion and supplies no continuous lower bound

scalar_mean_eincrement_comparison.source: exact continuous pair-cofire mean certificate plus fixed lambda=.036
scalar_mean_eincrement_comparison.interpretation: Deterministic population comparison only. The scalar mean increment remains the simpler primary candidate; the category-wise proposal is a valid alternative construction under the same certified null but is not shown to improve drift or decoder utility.

conditional_validity_argument: For any predictable exact-circuit null parameter in the declared rectangle, each category probability is at most its certified U_c. For any fixed proposal distribution q on the six categories, L(C)=q(C)/U_C is nonnegative and E[L|past]=sum_c P(C=c|past)q(c)/U_c <= sum_c q(c)=1. Thus it is a one-step e-factor under the exact stated conditional model; products (or predictable mixtures) form an e-process. This is a mathematical construction only, not an implemented or run detector.
limitations: Fixed gate noise and exact categorical circuit only; no correlated-readout, gate drift, model error, or unknown circuit topology.
The approximate DEM receives no continuous category-envelope certificate here.
Expected log increments are population calculations; no finite-history delay, ARL, switching risk, logical error, or decoder utility was evaluated.

Finite Bernstein subdivision yields rigorous upper bounds but may be conservative; a positive minimum log-growth is reported only on the specified alternative grid, not continuously over the alternative rectangle.
